newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on soy and weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on soy and weather.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a break in soybeans plus overall good wheat crop weather in the U.S., traders said.
"There was nothing bullish and funds sold it," a trader said.
USDA Monday said U.S. winter wheat crop conditions improved last week and further improvement was expected this week because of favorable crop weather, industry sources said.
Also there were some forecasts for showers early next week in the dry region of Kansas which would help crop prospects in that key hard red winter wheat state.
The wheat crop is beginning to head out in Kansas and showers are needed to help ensure an adequate crop.
Smith Barney, Refco Inc and LIT America each sold one million bushels of July, while Term Commodities sold two million July and Cargill Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of July.
Wheat closed two to 8-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down five at $3.83 and July was down 8-1/2 at $3.87.
In spread trading, FIMAT Futures did one million bushels of July/September at seven cents and R.J. O'Brien did one million July/September at seven cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 contracts, below the 23,266 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 400 July $4.30 calls at four to 4-1/2 cents, FCC bought 200 July $4.10 puts at 25-1/2 to 26 cents and E.D. and F. Man Interntional sold 200 July $4.30 puts at 41-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 11,203 traded Tuesday.
